title: Lifting high-power fibre sections on a proper algebraic space
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning one with a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]; proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $L$ be a line module on $X$, an $\mathcal O_X$-module on its small etale site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pullback along $a:Z\to W$ means $a^*M=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O_W}a^{-1}M$ in the canonical ringed etale topoi [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]; tensor powers use tensor product of module sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with $L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_X$. Fix $t\in T$, put $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, and write $L_t$ for the pulled-back line. Suppose $X_t$ is a scheme and the corresponding ordinary invertible module is ample [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence, def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There is an integer $d_0\geq0$ such that for every integer $d\geq d_0$ and every $v\in\Gamma(X_t,L_t^{\otimes d})$ there are an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq T$ of $t$ and $\widetilde v\in\Gamma(X_U,L^{\otimes d}|_{X_U})$ whose pullback is $v$, under the canonical tensor-pullback identification $(L^{\otimes d})_t\cong L_t^{\otimes d}$. Here $X_U=X\times_TU$, and $\Gamma$ denotes sections of the module sheaf (ordinary sections under the scheme comparison). The neighbourhood may depend on $d$ and $v$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), final surjectivity assertion specialized to F = O_X and expressed by representatives of direct-image germs on open neighbourhoods of t.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k=\kappa(t)$, and use the canonical flat morphism $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$. An affine Noetherian neighbourhood identifies $A$ with a localization of its Noetherian coordinate ring, so $A$ is Noetherian. Set $Z=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}A$, with projections $h:Z\to X$ and $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $N=h^*L$. Properness is preserved by this base change. Tensor pullback carries a local frame of $L$ to a frame of $N$; its tensor-power comparison sends a tensor of pulled-back sections to the pullback of their tensor. Thus $N$ is a line and its closed fibre with its line is canonically $(X_t,L_t)$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), proof with F = O_X, local-base reduction and final degree-zero argument via Tag 08AY(3).

proof.text: Let $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_Z$. The uniform conormal-vanishing input gives one $d_0\geq0$ with $H^1(Z,(J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes N^{\otimes d})=0$ for every $n\geq0$ and $d\geq d_0$. Its schematic closed-fibre and ampleness assumptions hold by the preceding identification. Fix such a $d$, and put $E=N^{\otimes d}$ and $Q_n=E/J^nE$ for $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), proof with F = O_X, local-base reduction and final degree-zero argument via Tag 08AY(3).

proof.text:
For every $n\geq1$ there is a short exact sequence
$$0\to (J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes E\to Q_{n+1}\to Q_n\to0.$$
Indeed, on a frame of $E$ this is the elementary quotient sequence $0\to J^n/J^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_Z/J^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_Z/J^n\to0$; changes of frame multiply all three terms by the same unit, so these sequences agree on overlaps. The closed fibre is cut out by $J$: on every affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Z$, base change to $k$ has ring $B\otimes_Ak=B/\mathfrak m B$. Hence $Q_1=i_*i^*E$, where $i:X_t\to Z$ is the closed immersion. The closed-immersion module statement identifies the quotient structure sheaf, and tensoring a frame gives this identification for $E$. In particular $\Gamma(Z,Q_1)=\Gamma(X_t,L_t^{\otimes d})$, by the definition of direct image and the tensor-power comparison.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), proof with F = O_X, local-base reduction and final degree-zero argument via Tag 08AY(3).

proof.text: Apply the long exact sequence of right derived global sections on the etale topos to each sequence above. Abelian sheaves have enough injectives; global sections is additive and left exact since kernels are computed sectionwise. The zero $H^1$ of the first term makes $\Gamma(Z,Q_{n+1})\to\Gamma(Z,Q_n)$ surjective. For any finite $r\geq1$, composing the $r-1$ surjections gives a surjection $\tau_{r,1}$; at $r=1$ it is the identity. No assertion about choosing an infinite compatible sequence is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), proof with F = O_X, local-base reduction and final degree-zero argument via Tag 08AY(3).

proof.text: Apply section-image stabilization to the proper local-base space $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the line $E$. For some finite $r\geq1$, $\operatorname{Im}(\rho_1)=\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{r,1})$. The latter is all of $\Gamma(Z,Q_1)$ by the preceding step. Therefore every prescribed fibre section $v$ has a preimage $w\in\Gamma(Z,E)$. This uses only stabilization in degree zero; it requires neither completeness of $A$ nor flatness of $g$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), proof with F = O_X, local-base reduction and final degree-zero argument via Tag 08AY(3).

proof.text: Write $M=L^{\otimes d}$. It is quasi-coherent because locally it is free of rank one. The direct image $f_*M$ is quasi-coherent, and flat base change along $c$ identifies $c^*f_*M$ with $g_*E$ by the canonical adjunction-mate map. Regard $f_*M$ as its ordinary quasi-coherent module $G$ on $T$ by the scheme comparison, which preserves pullback and sections on opens. The canonical local-morphism statement identifies $G_t$ with $(c^*G)_{\mathfrak m}$. Every open neighbourhood of the closed point in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the whole scheme: a basic open containing $\mathfrak m$ is defined by a unit. Thus this stalk equals global sections and, by base change, $\Gamma(Z,E)$. Represent the germ corresponding to $w$ by $\widetilde v\in G(U)=\Gamma(X_U,M)$ on an open $U\ni t$. The base-change map is the adjunction mate, so it takes this germ to the pullback of $\widetilde v$ on $Z$ (its formula is unit followed by the pulled-back counit). Restricting further to $X_t$ gives the image of $w$, namely $v$.
